transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump spoke with crowds in Florida today as part of his nationwide campaign tour
ahead of the midterm election.
He encouraged voters to get out and vote as if his name was on the ballot and PR's Maham
Javed has more.
The president encouraged his supporters to vote for Republican nominees for Florida's
gubernatorial and senate candidates, both of whom are ahead in their respective races.
So ladies and gentlemen of Florida, the golden age of America is upon us.
You must go out.
You must vote Republican.
Lucila Fedrowski came wearing a MAGA hat and a Gulf of America t-shirt.
She says it's important to vote against Democrats.
Now they're radical Democrats and they're crazy.
So we have to save our country because they're not the Democratic Party from your parents.
So please vote red.
She's a former Democrat and is excited to vote red down the ballot.
Maham Javed, NPR News, Fort Myers.
Two former FBI intelligence officials have been charged with lying about their roles
in investigating the origins of Hunter Biden's laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential
election.
The Justice Department says Nikki Flores and Bradley Benevide lied to Congress in 2023
about the involvement of a specialized foreign-influenced task force in investigations into Biden.
Flores's lawyers describe the case as nonsense.
The case marks the latest in a series of politically charged actions from the Justice Department
ahead of the midterm elections.
The Mississippi police officer who fired the shot that killed a black toddler while responding
to a shoplifting call in June has resigned.
That Hunter Foster's attorney says he had no choice but to shoot at the vehicle because
it was moving toward him.
The child's family says the shooting was not justified.
Elise Catrine Gregg of the Gulf States newsroom in Mississippi Public Broadcasting says body
cam footage of the lethal encounter has been released.
The officer who fired into the car, killing one-year-old Cohen Wiley in June, stepped
down following the release of the footage.
Police say the car was moving toward them, but Wiley's mother says that's not true.
Also shows that police surrounded the car, which began moving forward.
Officers pursued the car as it moved to the side.
Wiley family attorney Van Turner says they plan to file a civil suit.
They have been blocking the vehicle in the first place and putting themselves in harm's
way to then circle back around and say, hey, we're justified in putting the trigger in.
Authorities have cleared the officer, Hunter Foster, saying the shooting was justified.
For NPR News, I'm Elise Catrine Gregg in Jackson, Mississippi.
Another storm, Vance, has become a hurricane off the coast of Mexico and the Pacific.
Vance is a Category 2 hurricane with winds of up to 110 miles an hour and is expected
to strengthen rapidly to become a major Category 3 hurricane later today.
The Pacific hurricane season has been intense, with several storms forming near Hawaii and
Mexico.
This is NPR News.
Police attorneys for the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk are suggesting
a 2029 trial date and say they need years to prepare for their case.
Tyler Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder.
President Trump criticized the judge prior to the hearing and said the case should be
tried within a month.
American conductor and composer Julian Walker has been indicted on federal child pornography
charges.
Secretary Harris on Associate Silkes reports Walker was spared prison on charges at the
state level.
The federal charges include four counts of receiving child pornography and a count of
possessing child pornography.
Videos included in the indictment show multiple children under the age of 12 being sexually
abused.
At the time of Julian Walker's initial arrest last year, he was teaching fourth grade at
an Indianapolis school.
Last month, he avoided a prison sentence after pleading guilty to five counts of possession
of child sex abuse material and one count of possession of cocaine.
He was sentenced to nearly six years of probation and registered as a sex offender.
He is pleaded not guilty to the federal charges.
Walker was nominated for two Grammy Awards and has conducted major orchestras around
the world.
If convicted on the federal charges, he could face up to 20 years in prison.
On Estazia Zilkes, NPR News.
Some Airbnb guests may soon have fewer chores to tackle before checking out.
The short-term rental platform says it is changing its rules to limit what hosts can
require of guests.
The new policy says hosts can no longer ask guests to wash dishes, strip barrette beds
or take out the trash.
This is NPR News.
